desc: Ideation: derive sweep with prefix distinct P, suffix distinct S, last-occurrence range updates, and lazy segment tree for range-add/range-max.

Implement the complete O(N log N) Python solution: fast stdin parsing, prefix/suffix distinct arrays, iterative lazy segment tree over left cuts initialized to P[i], sweep j with range add/query, and print the maximum.
Validate edge cases mentally or with small brute checks: N=3, all equal values, all distinct values, repeated values crossing both cuts, and off-by-one on S[j+1].
If the lazy segment tree is too slow in Python, switch to a PyPy-friendly iterative implementation or equivalent O(N log N)/O(N) optimization.

**Update rule**: When `x = A[j]` is appended to the middle, it is newly distinct exactly for left cuts `i >= prev[x]` (previous occurrence, 0 if none). The code applies `+1` on `[max(1, prev), j-1]` — correct.

**Segment tree invariant**: `tree[p] = true_subtree_max - (lazy on strict ancestors)` is maintained because (a) canonical nodes of the range add get `tree += 1, lazy += 1`, (b) all partial-overlap nodes lie on the two boundary root-to-leaf paths and are rebuilt as `max(children) + lazy[p]`, and (c) only `tree[1]` (no ancestors) is ever read. The activation proof holds: any node with pending lazy lies entirely inside a past update range ending `<= R-1`, so ancestors of the newly activated leaf `R` have lazy 0, making plain leaf assignment valid.
**Hand traces**: Sample 1 → 5 ✓, Sample 2 → 9 ✓ (full trace: candidates 7,7,8,8,9,9,9,8), N=3 all-distinct → 3 ✓, all-equal N=5 → 3 ✓, all-distinct N=5 → 5 ✓.

**Edge details**: `S[j+1]` indexing correct (S[n] defined); loop `j in range(2, n)` guarantees `1 <= i < j <= N-1` with all parts non-empty; `last[x]` read before being overwritten; NEG = -10^18 safely below any real value.
